description.narrative: Amidst the unprecedented surge in violence in Gaza gripping the West Bank, the stringent movement restrictions enforced through theinstallation of metal gates and cement blocks at key entry points to cities, villages, and refugee camps have wrought profound consequences on the daily lives of Palestinians. These measures, indicative of the heightened tensions, have resulted in severe impediments to accessing essential services, goods, and even water, exacerbating an already dire humanitarian crisis. Furthermore, the plight of Palestinian men and women workers who once found employment in Israel, now facing the consequences of their sudden loss of employment last October and lack of opportunities in the West Bank due to the increased movement restrictions and closure of businesses,serves as a stark reminder of the socio-economic fallout precipitated by the escalating violence. This is especially true for women-headed households and working women, where women face double burdens of providing for their families and maintaining all household care and childcare duties in the context of limited available and accessible income-generating opportunities. Dire economic situations may also increase the risk of early marriage for girls. The severe restrictions on movement and borders not only exacerbate the humanitarian crisis but also disrupt the import and export of essential commodities, leading to prolonged supply chains and increasedtransportation costs. Consequently, this disruption amplifies economic instability, diminishing the purchasing power of men and women, and further unravelling the socio-economic fabric of the West Bank, over 40% of Palestinian SMES have closed their business since October 7th in WB. In the aftermath of the Gaza war in October 2023, the situation in the West Bank has worsened for Palestinian landowners. Severe restrictions imposed by an Israeli military coordination system aim to curb settler violence. However, these restrictions limit landowners' access to their lands, allowing only short periods for planting and harvesting. Consequently, crops are left vulnerable to encroachment and theft by settlers. The recent cancellation of this coordination mechanism has intensified the situation, especially impacting olive harvests near settlements and in remote areas. The lack of Israeli intervention against settler harassment perpetuates violence, severely affecting the livelihoods of thousands of Palestinian families. Palestinian women bear additional burdens and risks, as they face the consequences of Israeli occupation policies and entrenched patriarchal social norms. Womenworkers and farmers are particularly vulnerable to various forms of sexual harassment and exploitation at checkpoints and from Israeli settlers..

participating-org.narrative: In 1983 a small group of agronomists founded the Palestinian Agricultural Relief Committees (PARC), which has since developed into one of the most important Palestinian non-governmental organisations providing services to poor and marginalised farmers onthe West Bank and Gaza Strip, working to make agricultural businesses grow. PARC#s goal is to promote an economic and social climate that would allow the Palestinian agricultural sector to develop sustainably. Another goal is to improve the living standard of Palestinians living in rural areas, especially of poor farming families. PARC provides a broad range of agricultural extension services. It is active in land reclamation and in building rural access roads. The organisation advocates the improvementof rural women#s economic position. It is part of an Oxfam Novib-funded three-year gender-focus program. In 1991 PARC got an ISO-certification. It was the first and so far only non-governmental organisation in the Arab world to obtain one. It has also developed an impressive strategic ten-year plan for the 1998-2008 period. Together with several other agricultural non-governmental organisations (NGOs) PARC has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Ministry of Agriculture, which sees PARC#s workasindependent and complementary to its own. PARC is active in a network of Palestinian NGOs and a member of the governing committee of the Palestinian NGO-network. Oxfam Novib has been supporting PARC since 1982. In 1999 Oxfam Novib, ICCO, Christian Aid (UK) and Oxfam Great Britain set up a donor consortium to support PARC. This provides PARC a measure of long-term financial security. It also makes technical and organisational assistance available to PARC in further developing its program.
